items.action: Patch NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances per Citrix guidance, or isolate/shut down internet-facing units until fixed; preserve logs and snapshots as evidence of possible prior compromise.
items.details: CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 27 with a federal remediation deadline of September 30. Security firm watchTowr confirmed active exploitation on September 26; both flaws score CVSS v4.0 9.5.
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated arbitrary command execution) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory-buffer RCE/DoS) to its KEV catalog after watchTowr confirmed the flaws are being actively exploited against NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances.
items.title: Citrix NetScaler RCE flaws added to CISA KEV amid active exploitation

items.action: Apply Oracle's patches for CVE-2026-35273 immediately; disable the EMHub service or remove the PSEMHUB app, and hunt WebLogic logs for requests to /PSEMHUB/ or percent-encoded variants like /%50SEMHUB/.
items.details: Mandiant notified over 100 organizations in the first wave; web shells were found on dozens of systems across education, tech, IT services, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, and government.
items.summary: UNC6240 (ShinyHunters-linked) resumed mass exploitation of the critical CVE-2026-35273 (CVSS 9.8) pre-auth RCE flaw by requesting /%50SEMHUB/ instead of /PSEMHUB/, slipping past WAF rules that match the literal path before URL decoding.
items.title: ShinyHunters resume Oracle PeopleSoft attacks with one-character WAF bypass

items.action: Apply Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday SharePoint updates immediately and hunt SharePoint servers for webshell artifacts and suspicious activity by low-privilege accounts.
items.details: Early-warning platform Previdian observed exploitation attempts on September 24 and webshell backdoor creation attempts on September 25, with in-the-wild exploits based on Viettel Security's technical writeup. This is the eighth SharePoint flaw added to CISA KEV in 2026.
items.summary: CVE-2026-65660, a code-injection RCE flaw (CVSS 8.8) in Microsoft SharePoint Server, is being exploited in the wild just two days after Viettel Security published technical details; CISA added it to KEV on September 25 with a federal remediation deadline of today, September 28.
items.title: SharePoint CVE-2026-65660 exploited in the wild; CISA patch deadline hits today

items.action: Update internet-exposed RouterOS 7.x builds immediately, remove or restrict admin exposure from the internet, and review logs for unauthorized session activity.
items.details: CERT Polska and Bishop Fox confirmed the MikroTrick exploit bypasses authentication entirely by combining a session channel creation flaw with a login policy mask injection. CISA added both CVEs to KEV on September 25 with a September 28 remediation deadline.
items.summary: The 'MikroTrick' exploit chain combines CVE-2026-67279 with CVE-2026-86060 to grant full unauthenticated administrative control of vulnerable MikroTik RouterOS 7.x devices; both flaws are now on CISA's KEV list.
items.title: 'MikroTrick' chain gives unauthenticated admin access on exposed MikroTik routers

items.details: Exposed datasets included private conversations from an Indian adult streaming site, thousands of US valet license plates, and contact details from an immigration service. Supabase says projects are secure by default but called security a shared responsibility, noting customers control how their databases are configured.
items.summary: UpGuard identified 16,326 Supabase-hosted databases with publicly readable tables; over half showed indicators of personally identifiable information, and a smaller share exposed passwords and authentication tokens. The root cause is Postgres row-level security being off by default for tables created via SQL, including AI coding tools.
items.title: 16,300+ Supabase databases leaking personal data to the open web

items.details: First Secure Bank Group is a U.S. community bank headquartered in Joliet, Illinois, offering personal and business banking, lending, and mortgages through First Secure Bank and The State Bank Group.
items.summary: The Storm ransomware group publicly claimed responsibility for an attack on First Secure Bank Group on September 27, raising the risk that customer financial data was exfiltrated and could be published.
items.title: Storm ransomware claims attack on First Secure Bank Group

items.details: No technical entry point, data volume, or operational impact details were provided in the claim; disclosure reflects the victim's appearance on the group's leak site.
items.summary: The Qilin ransomware group listed Revenga Smart Solutions as a new victim on its leak site on September 27; the scale of any breach remains unconfirmed.
items.title: Qilin ransomware lists Revenga Smart Solutions as victim

items.details: Ressources Si is described as a small business in the movie theater industry with 10-19 employees; Panzer employs a double-extortion model of exfiltrating data before encrypting.
items.summary: The Panzer ransomware group listed Ressources Si on its leak site on September 27, claiming the exfiltration of 100GB of data; customers and employees should watch for phishing or misuse of personal information.
items.title: Panzer ransomware claims 100GB data theft from Ressources Si

items.details: Disclosure reflects the victim's appearance on Incransom's dark web leak site; the initial compromise date is unknown.
items.summary: The Incransom ransomware group claimed nsbsd.org, a U.S. organization in the government and defense sector, as a victim on September 28 via its leak site.
items.title: Incransom ransomware claims breach of nsbsd.org

items.action: Government agencies should audit web-facing assets for unauthorized changes and defacements, and confirm the incident has been reported to the Cyber Police.
items.details: The Kerala State IT Mission operates key Keralam government websites and e-governance programmes. Officials said the website will be restored after security checks are completed, and a similar defacement of kerala.gov.in by a group claiming to be the Pakistan Cyber Army occurred in September 2015.
items.summary: The official website of Keralam's General Administration Department was hacked on September 27; attackers posted a Pakistani flag and a message claiming to be 'Team Blackleets'. The hosting provider suspended the account and a cyber team is examining whether any data was compromised.
items.title: Keralam GAD website defaced by suspected Pakistani group 'Team Blackleets'
